reasons: Classification is correct: § 2.1 is a three-year, USD 2,000,000/year take-or-pay with no reduction or termination right, which is expressly the rule's walk-away position and fails the fallback (12-month term, 30-day reduction right, true-up rather than penalty), so a deviation finding with a redline is warranted.

The redline is directionally right and actionable: it removes the take-or-pay and substitutes pay-for-usage-or-ordered-Services language, matching the preferred position, and the redline guidance expressly permits deletion as well as narrowing.

The advisory minimal-edit failure (0.975 changed-character ratio) is acceptable here because the offending obligation is the entire substance of the paragraph; there is no smaller edit that removes a walk-away take-or-pay commitment.

Comment is accurate, concise and in the required voice, states what changed and why, and offers the 12-month/30-day/true-up fallback as a negotiation position. Cross-references to §§ 9.4 and 12.3 are supporting context only and do not carry the finding; recommend a quick sanity check that those section numbers are quoted correctly before sending.
